translit: tān samīkṣhya sa kaunteyaḥ sarvān bandhūn avasthitān
theme: When Love Makes Our Hands Tremble
hindi: दोनों सेनाओं में खड़े अपने ससुर, मित्रों और सब संबंधियों को देखकर कुंतीपुत्र अर्जुन गहरी करुणा से भर गए। वे बहुत दुखी हुए और उदास मन से यह बोले।
english: Arjuna, son of Kunti, looked at all his relatives and friends standing in both armies, including his fathers-in-law and well-wishers. His heart filled with deep pity and sadness, and he spoke these words sorrowfully.
deeper: Until now Arjuna was ready and brave. But when he looked closely, he did not see “enemies”. He saw people he knew and loved. The verse shows the moment his heart began to change. The word kṛpā means tender compassion, and here it is so strong that it makes him sink into sadness (viṣīdan).

Notice that the verse says he was “overcome” (āviṣṭaḥ). Love and kindness are beautiful. But when a feeling becomes so big that it covers our thinking, we can lose our way. Arjuna’s feeling is real and human, and the Gita never laughs at it. It also shows us that a warm feeling alone cannot always tell us what the right action is.

This is why the verse ends with “he spoke these words”. Arjuna is about to share his trouble honestly. Telling our confusion to a wise friend or guide is the first step to clearing it. Krishna will listen and then teach.
words: feeling sad and sinking in heart
background: Arjuna had asked Krishna to place the chariot between the two armies so he could see who stood ready to fight (1.21–1.23). Krishna drew up the chariot right in front of Bhishma and Drona and said, “Partha, look at all these Kurus gathered here” (1.24–1.25).

Arjuna looked and saw grandfathers, teachers, uncles, brothers, sons, friends and well-wishers on both sides (1.26). Now, in this verse, he sees them all clearly. His heart is touched by pity and he starts to speak. His words begin in the next verse.
lessons: Arjuna took a long, careful look and saw real people, not just a crowd.
Feeling tender for others shows a good heart, and it is a strength.
When sadness or fear is too strong, it is hard to see what we should do.
Arjuna did not hide his heart. Sharing our worry is the first step to peace.
Arjuna had Krishna beside him. We too should turn to elders and teachers when confused.
examples: Rohan’s team plays the final against his cousin’s team. When he sees cousin Vikram smiling from the other side, he suddenly does not feel like playing hard.
Meera is told to compete in a class debate. She looks at her classmates and realises each one is a friend with feelings. She feels a little worried about winning.
In the school quiz, the teachers’ team sits opposite the students. Ananya admires them so much that she feels shy about answering before them.
Kabir feels heavy because of a quarrel with his best friend. He tells Amma everything at dinner, and his heart feels lighter.
Sneha sees a shivering puppy outside the gate on a rainy day. Her heart fills with pity, and she runs to ask her father for an old towel.
Arjun sees his friend crying before the exam. His own mind gets so upset that he forgets the answers he knew well. Later he learns to calm down first.
In the family sports day, Diya has to run against her little brother. She slows down out of love, and then wonders whether that was really the kind thing to do.
Farhan is confused about whether to tell the teacher about a friend’s mistake. Instead of deciding alone, he asks his grandfather for advice.

story.title: Tara and the Chess Final
paras: Tara loved chess. She worked hard all year, and at last she reached the school final. When she sat down at the board, she looked up and saw her own cousin Karan sitting across from her. He had taught her the very first moves when she was small.
Tara’s heart filled with warmth and worry. “What if he feels bad when he loses? What if I feel bad when I win?” Her hand shook over the pieces. She could not even decide whether to move a pawn.

At the break, her teacher, Sunita Ma’am, saw her pale face and asked what was wrong. Tara told her everything. Ma’am smiled gently. “Your love for Karan is lovely, Tara. But a fair game is also a way of respecting him. He wants a real match, not a gift.”

Tara took a deep breath and went back. She played honestly and with a calm heart. She lost one game and won one, and in the end she and Karan shared a huge laddoo and laughed. She understood that love and duty do not have to fight each other when we think clearly.
story.moral: Lesson: Feelings of love are precious, but when they make us freeze, we should speak up and seek wise guidance.

quiz.q: What did Arjuna see when he looked at both armies?
quiz.x: He saw many people close to him standing in both armies.

quiz.q: What feeling filled Arjuna’s heart in this verse?
quiz.x: The verse says he was overcome with deep compassion and felt sad.
Kṛpā means tender pity or compassion for others.

quiz.q: What is a good thing to do when a big feeling makes us confused?
o: Share it with a wise elder or guide
quiz.x: Arjuna spoke his trouble to Krishna, and we too should talk to someone wise.

reel.hook: What if the “opponent” is someone you love? 💔
reel.lesson: Compassion is beautiful, but share your confusion with a wise guide.
reel.caption:
Arjuna looked at the faces across the battlefield and his heart melted. 💔
Big feelings are okay, and so is asking for guidance.
Who do you turn to when you feel confused? 🌼
